mu_name_from: MuMain maps MODEL_HELM + i to the file at i+1; file 10 is index 9, which openmu names Plate.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateArmor(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)`, so slot 2 is group 7, 3 is 8 and 4 is 9.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 1, 0 - the Dark Knight alone.
stats.shelf_note: On Martin's and Harold's shelf at +3 - the last column of the wandering merchants' stock, see shared/Market.cs - and until this row existed the shelf dropped the line, because a model with no row is a thing the realm cannot price. The five Plate pieces were built for the guards' bodies first and the row came second.

sheet_from: MuMain/src/bin/Data/Player - the tree that was not upscaled in place.
sheet_note: Three sheets. guard_hair is a 32x32 TGA with real alpha - a cut-out plume - and nothing in the chain handles transparency yet, so it will bake as an opaque patch until it does.
cutout_from: MU does not keep this in the file. Data/Player/guard_hair.ozt - the plume - stores 0 in the alpha byte of all 1024 of its texels while holding perfectly good colour, so read literally it says draw none of it, and the client plainly draws it. The old client's model loader carries a BlendMeshIndex instead: a mesh named in code as the one to draw see-through. That is a statement about this model rather than a channel anyone can read, so it is stated here.
cutout_note: The feather is painted on near-black and the black is the part that is not there. So the mask is keyed off brightness rather than off the alpha channel that has nothing in it, and the result is alpha-tested rather than blended - a plume is two quads crossing at a right angle, which is the case that has no correct draw order.
material_note:
Three islands and two answers. Island 2 is 38 triangles - head_11's 35 and hide's 3, the great helm itself - and takes plate_steel. Islands 0 and 1 are two triangles each, which is guard_hair's 4 exactly: the plume, on two quads crossing at a right angle, and they take feather.

It shipped as plate_steel until the Bone set's own hair was noticed. A feather at metallic 1.0 is a black chrome fan, which is the fault hair.json was written to record on the Dark Knight's bare head - and the bare heads have had it right all along, each splitting skin from hair at the island. The plume is the same case on a helm, and the island is already separate, so nothing here is a limit.

The Bone Helm is where it is a limit: its six triangles of head_a06 are welded into the helm's own shell by shared vertices, so they cannot be given hair without finer assignment than an island. See HelmMale05's material_note.
